{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZhEGJA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDIGKw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 75, "title": "Implement edge-triggered PIC latching for the Ap shared OPNA/PCM IRQ", "body": "## Problem

The Ap sound path repeatedly requests slave IR4 while its shared OPNA/PCM output remains asserted. After acknowledgement clears IRR4, another scheduler tick latches a duplicate request without a new input edge. This can produce an extra interrupt after EOI and affects DOS sound-driver interrupt handling.

At baseline `b4897044fdf844028e179537ccc3d8f17e79594a`, [Bus::tick](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b4897044/src/bus.rs#L308) calls `Pic::request(4)` on every asserted sample; [Pic::request](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b4897044/src/devices.rs#L38) unconditionally sets IRR. The [original OPNA probe](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b4897044/guest/opna_irq.asm#L161) explicitly drains this extra request with polling and another EOI pair.

## Expected outcome

Implement logical edge detection for this one shared sound input under the existing edge-triggered, normal-EOI configuration:

- An inactive-to-active input transition latches a request; a continuously asserted input produces no additional request across acknowledgement, polling or EOI.
- Acknowledgement clears the selected IRR bit and sets ISR; ordinary cascade service requires EOI on both controllers.
- Following PIC initialization, a continuously asserted input must not fabricate a new edge.

These contracts follow Intel’s [8259A edge-triggered mode and initialization descriptions](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=17), [initialization sequence](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=9), and [acknowledgement/EOI descriptions](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=7).

Retain the existing combined logical assertion:

`opn.irq() || (pcm.irq && pcm.control & 0x20 != 0)`

Detect transitions after combining the sources. Adding or clearing one contributor while another remains asserted must not manufacture an edge. Yamaha’s [YM2608 Application Manual §2-2-1, translated transcription](https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/YM2608J_Translated.PDF#page=19) documents register-29 IRQ enables; preserve #73’s flag/enables separation.

Observe relevant guest port writes and clock-driven source changes, including PCM threshold changes during audio sampling. Back-to-back disable/re-enable writes must remain observable without an intervening `Bus::tick`.

## Context and reproduction

Source-level reproduction for the Coordinator:

1. Initialize the existing cascade with slave base `18h`, normal EOI, and IR4 unmasked.
2. Program a real OPNA timer overflow through guest ports, then stop counting while retaining its enabled flag.
3. Acknowledge vector `1Ch`, advance clocks with the source still asserted, and issue both EOIs.
4. Inspect IRR and poll responses. Current routing creates another request; the expected responses are empty until a subsequent input transition.

[Existing sound tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b4897044/tests/sound86.rs#L239) cover suppression, retention and recovery, but do not reject a continuously asserted source being requested again after acknowledgement.

Progress assessment: #74 resolves the bounded register-29 reset/enable gap. The [Coordinator’s validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b4897044/docs/validation.md#issue-73-ym2608-timer-irq-enables-2026-10-24) reports 302 native integration and 106 production-Wasm browser passes. Independent review and remote CI outcomes were not supplied. This evaluator inspected source, the core diff and reports; it executed no builds/tests, prepared no fixtures and changed no files.

No open Issues were supplied. This task extends neither #63’s polling implementation nor #73’s register semantics; it fixes their exposed device-to-PIC routing prerequisite.

Scope is the Ap shared sound input and its existing cascade integration. Preserve register-29 behavior, logical IRR retention, board I/O gating, PCM playback and existing VM behavior. Timer-frequency/prescaler reconciliation, other device inputs, level-triggered operation, electrical/spurious-interrupt timing and broad PIC refactoring are outside this Issue.

All 26 fixed inventory categories retain their supplied scopes and statuses: 23 partial, GRCG implemented/unverified, paging and FPU unimplemented. PIC remains partial after this task: SNGL/general ICW sequencing, programmable ICW3 routing, SFNM, level triggering, spurious interrupts, and broader polling/AEOI/rotation/concurrent-acknowledgement acceptance remain outstanding. Protected execution, paging and basic x87 remain required future work. Limited probes and six-game reports establish neither complete hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add an original Rust regression that fails on the baseline’s repeated-request behavior and passes unchanged after the routing fix. Generate timer flags through ports and elapsed clocks, not direct flag or PIC-request injection.
- [ ] Cover Timer A, Timer B and real PCM FIFO threshold interrupts independently; verify held-input behavior with CPU acknowledgement and normal-EOI polling, and recovery after a genuine inactive-to-active transition.
- [ ] Cover overlapping OPNA/PCM contributors in both orders, register-29 pending-flag toggles, PCM acknowledgement/refill, masked capture/unmasking, a new transition during service, and unchanged latched IRR/ISR when a source is suppressed. Include consecutive control writes without ticks.
- [ ] Check clock partitioning around timer overflow and PCM threshold crossing, including source observation after audio sampling. Check PIC reinitialization while asserted, independent Machine instances, and Machine reset followed by successful fresh delivery. Preserve existing timer-frequency expectations without treating them as newly verified hardware timing.
- [ ] Strengthen `guest/opna_irq.asm`: retain both timer paths and exactly four actual handler entries, but keep enabled recovery asserted across ordinary EOIs and a bounded guest delay. Assert that all eight recorded master/slave poll bytes are zero; remove the extra cleanup EOI pair. Retain suppression/retention checks, stack checks and all 128 result/guard comparisons. The baseline must fail the strengthened assertion.
- [ ] Update the independent builder oracle, checked provenance manifest, native test and browser expectations together. Preserve original MIT source, offline assembly commands, source/image hashes, unchanged media, PASS/FAIL checks and the existing 500,000-slot budget. Hosts may mount, step, reset and inspect; they must not inject interrupts or results.
- [ ] Run the identical source-built probe natively and through production release-Wasm at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, before and after reset. Keep fixture preparation wired into pre-merge acceptance CI. No proprietary firmware, samples or commercial guest acquisition is required.
- [ ] The Coordinator prepares the documented original/licensed prerequisites and passes `cargo test --locked --test sound86 --test pic --test ap --test music`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `npm test`. Preserve existing DOS/application, VM, CPU-shadow, PIT, PIC, audio and six-game assertions and budgets.
- [ ] Update hardware/probe documentation to remove the obsolete drain workaround. Record exact Coordinator/CI commands, outcomes and any failures; distinguish this bounded routing result from remaining PIC/OPNA gaps. Complete repository-required review before merge.

None.

None.
